I am 66 years old, and these 9 mu in Quzhou have been my life for 40 years. My wife and I work them alone, so every decision must balance our backs against the income. It is early spring now; the wheat I sowed last October is greening up, and I am thinking through the full year.

For the wheat, I have 7 mu down with an improved variety — I have shifted toward Luyuan 502 in recent years because it resists lodging and the stripe rust we get here. I rotary-tilled before sowing and applied compound fertilizer as basal. Now, as the season starts, I will topdress nitrogen at the jointing stage and irrigate three times total: once to help it through any late dry cold, again at jointing, and once more at grain filling. I keep chemicals to a minimum but will spray three times — herbicide early, then a fungicide and insecticide when the weather turns humid in May.

Come early June, the wheat comes off, and there is no time to lose before the summer rains arrive. I will no-till plant Denghai 605 hybrid maize the same day or the next day into the wheat stubble. No-tillage is the only way two old people can manage 7 mu in that narrow window; it also keeps the soil cooler and holds moisture when the July heat hits. I will fertilize with compound at sowing and side-dress urea at the big trumpet stage, irrigating twice if the summer rains fail.

Cotton is where the money per mu can be good, but it is cruel on the body — bending for pruning, carrying tanks for sprays. With only my wife and me, I limit cotton to 2 mu. I will rotary-till that plot when the soil warms in April and sow Guoxinmian hybrid. Cotton drinks more than people think, so I will irrigate three times through flowering and boll-setting. The bollworm is my biggest enemy, and I will stay vigilant with five well-timed sprays rather than letting an outbreak force me into a dozen panic applications. After 40 years and with the education I have, I read the labels, calibrate the sprayer, and know that more sprays do not always mean more profit.

My target is straightforward: 500 kg/mu of wheat, 600 kg/mu of maize, and 280 kg/mu of seed cotton. These are yields I have hit before, and with well water and discipline, I will hit them again.
